stem: The system that transports substances like food, oxygen and wastes in the human body is the __________.
solution: The circulatory system transports food, oxygen, carbon dioxide and wastes around the body.

stem: The main pumping organ of the circulatory system is the __________.
solution: The heart pumps blood throughout the body.

stem: The fluid that flows through blood vessels and transports substances is __________.
solution: Blood is the transporting fluid of the circulatory system.

stem: The red colour of blood is due to a pigment called __________.
solution: Haemoglobin, present in red blood cells, gives blood its red colour and carries oxygen.

stem: The blood cells that carry oxygen are the __________.
solution: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds and carries oxygen.

stem: The blood cells that fight infection and protect the body are the __________.
solution: White blood cells defend the body against germs and infections.

stem: The cell fragments that help in clotting of blood are the __________.
solution: Platelets help blood clot at wounds, preventing excessive bleeding.

stem: The liquid part of blood in which cells float is called __________.
solution: Plasma is the pale-yellow liquid part of blood that carries cells and dissolved substances.

stem: Blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart are called __________.
solution: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, usually oxygen-rich blood.

stem: Blood vessels that carry blood back to the heart are called __________.
solution: Veins carry blood back to the heart, usually oxygen-poor blood.

stem: The smallest, thin-walled blood vessels where exchange of substances occurs are the __________.
solution: Capillaries are tiny, thin-walled vessels that allow exchange of gases and nutrients with tissues.

stem: The rhythmic throbbing felt in an artery due to the heartbeat is the __________.
solution: The pulse is the throbbing felt in arteries with each heartbeat; it equals the heart rate.

stem: The normal pulse (heart) rate of a resting adult is about __________ beats per minute.
solution: A resting adult's heart beats about 70–72 times per minute.

stem: Arteries have thick, elastic walls because they __________.
options: carry blood at high pressure from the heart
solution: Arteries have thick, elastic walls to withstand the high pressure of blood pumped by the heart.

stem: Veins have valves to __________.
solution: Valves in veins ensure blood flows only towards the heart, preventing backflow.

stem: The removal of harmful metabolic wastes from the body is called __________.
solution: Excretion is the removal of metabolic waste products from the body.

stem: The main excretory organs in humans that filter blood to make urine are the __________.
solution: The kidneys filter the blood, removing wastes as urine.

stem: The nitrogenous waste removed by the kidneys in urine is mainly __________.
solution: Urea is the main nitrogenous waste filtered out by the kidneys and excreted in urine.

stem: Sweat produced by the skin helps in excretion and also in __________.
solution: Sweating removes some water and salts (excretion) and cools the body as sweat evaporates.

stem: Water and minerals are transported in plants through the __________.
solution: Xylem tissue transports water and dissolved minerals from the roots up to the leaves.

stem: Food prepared in the leaves is transported to other parts of the plant through the __________.
solution: Phloem transports the food (sugars) made in leaves to the rest of the plant.

stem: The loss of water in the form of vapour from the aerial parts (mainly leaves) of a plant is called __________.
solution: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaves, mainly through stomata.

stem: Transpiration is useful to a plant because it helps in __________.
options: pulling water and minerals up from the roots (transpiration pull)
solution: Transpiration creates a suction (transpiration pull) that draws water and minerals up from the roots.

stem: Water absorbed by roots is drawn upward mainly due to __________.
solution: Transpiration pull (and root pressure) moves water upward through the xylem against gravity.

stem: The tiny root structures that absorb water and minerals from the soil are the __________.
solution: Root hairs increase the surface area of roots to absorb water and minerals efficiently.

stem: The human heart is divided into __________ chambers.
solution: The human heart has four chambers — two atria (upper) and two ventricles (lower).

stem: The upper chambers of the heart are called __________.
solution: The two upper chambers of the heart are the atria (auricles) that receive blood.

stem: The lower chambers of the heart, which pump blood out, are the __________.
solution: The two ventricles are the lower chambers that pump blood out of the heart.

stem: Dialysis is a procedure used when a person's __________ fail.
solution: Dialysis artificially filters the blood to remove wastes when the kidneys fail.

stem: The instrument used by doctors to listen to heart sounds is the __________.
solution: A stethoscope is used to listen to the sounds of the heartbeat.

stem: In aquatic plants and simple organisms, transport can occur mainly by __________.
solution: In small or simple organisms, substances move directly by diffusion without a special transport system.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a blood component with its function?
solution: Red blood cells carry oxygen. (WBCs fight germs, platelets clot blood, plasma transports substances.)

stem: The blood carries digested food from the intestine to __________.
solution: Blood transports absorbed nutrients from the intestine to all cells of the body.

stem: The pulse is best felt at the __________.
solution: The pulse can be conveniently felt where an artery is near the skin, such as at the wrist or neck.

stem: During excretion, the lungs remove __________ from the body.
solution: The lungs excrete carbon dioxide and some water vapour during exhalation.

stem: The transport of water in tall trees can occur to great heights mainly because of __________.
options: continuous transpiration pull through the xylem
solution: Transpiration pull continuously draws water up the xylem to the tops of even very tall trees.

stem: Blood flows through the body in a continuous system of __________.
solution: Blood circulates through a closed network of arteries, veins and capillaries.

stem: Which process helps aquatic animals get rid of wastes directly into water?
options: Diffusion of wastes across their body surface/gills
solution: Many aquatic animals remove wastes by diffusion into the surrounding water, e.g., through gills.

stem: The excretory unit of the kidney that filters blood is the __________.
solution: The nephron is the filtering unit of the kidney; each kidney has many nephrons.

stem: Which of the following is transported by the phloem?
solution: Phloem transports food (sugars) from the leaves to storage and growing parts of the plant.

stem: Excess water lost by transpiration is replaced by __________.
solution: Water lost by transpiration is continuously replaced by water absorbed from the soil by the roots.

stem: A person who has lost a lot of blood may be given __________.
solution: A blood transfusion replaces lost blood in a person who has bled heavily.

stem: Which of the following statements about the heart is TRUE?
options: It beats continuously throughout life to pump blood
solution: The heart beats continuously throughout life, pumping blood without a long rest.

stem: The circulatory system carries oxygen from the lungs to body cells and brings back __________.
solution: Blood carries oxygen from the lungs to cells and returns carbon dioxide to the lungs to be exhaled.

stem: Root pressure is greatest and helps push water up when __________.
options: transpiration is low, such as at night
solution: At night, when transpiration is low, root pressure plays a larger role in pushing water upward.

stem: Which of the following animals has a well-developed circulatory system with a heart?
solution: Complex animals like humans have a heart and blood vessels; simple organisms rely on diffusion.

stem: The main function of blood is to __________.
options: transport substances such as oxygen, nutrients and wastes
solution: Blood transports oxygen, nutrients, hormones and wastes throughout the body.

stem: Sweating on a hot day increases; this helps in __________.
options: removing wastes and cooling the body
solution: Increased sweating removes water and salts (excretion) and cools the body by evaporation.

stem: The transport of oxygen in the blood is carried out mainly by __________.
solution: Haemoglobin in red blood cells binds and carries oxygen to the body's cells.

stem: The rhythmic contraction and relaxation of the heart that pumps blood is called the __________.
solution: The heartbeat is the rhythmic contraction and relaxation of the heart muscle that pumps blood.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Transportation in Animals and Plants' is that:
options: living organisms have systems to transport substances (blood/circulatory system in animals; xylem and phloem in plants) and to remove wastes
solution: The chapter explains transport of materials by the circulatory system in animals and by xylem/phloem in plants, along with excretion of wastes.

stem: The system that transports materials like food, oxygen and waste in the human body is the:
solution: The circulatory (transport) system, consisting of the heart, blood and blood vessels, transports oxygen, digested food, waste products and other materials throughout the body.

stem: The fluid connective tissue that transports substances in the body is:
solution: Blood is the fluid connective tissue that transports oxygen, carbon dioxide, digested food, hormones and waste products, and helps fight infection and regulate temperature.

stem: The red pigment in blood that carries oxygen is:
solution: Haemoglobin, present in the red blood cells, is a red pigment that binds and carries oxygen from the lungs to all parts of the body.

stem: The blood cells that carry oxygen and give blood its red colour are the:
solution: Red blood cells (RBCs) contain haemoglobin, which carries oxygen and gives blood its red colour.

stem: The blood cells that fight infection and protect the body from disease are the:
solution: White blood cells (WBCs) are part of the body's defence system; they fight infections and destroy disease-causing germs.

stem: The blood cells that help in the clotting of blood (to stop bleeding) are the:
solution: Platelets help in the clotting of blood at the site of a wound, stopping bleeding and preventing excessive blood loss.

stem: The liquid part of the blood in which cells float is called:
solution: Plasma is the pale-yellow liquid part of the blood in which the blood cells (RBCs, WBCs, platelets) float; it carries dissolved substances like nutrients and waste.

stem: The muscular organ that pumps blood throughout the body is the:
solution: The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood continuously throughout the body via the blood vessels, keeping the circulation going.

stem: The human heart has how many chambers?
solution: The human heart has four chambers — two upper atria (auricles) and two lower ventricles — which keep oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor blood separate.

stem: The blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart to the body are the:
solution: Arteries carry blood away from the heart to the body (usually oxygen-rich blood, except the pulmonary artery); they have thick, elastic walls to withstand high pressure.

stem: The blood vessels that carry blood from the body back to the heart are the:
solution: Veins carry blood from the body back to the heart (usually oxygen-poor blood, except the pulmonary vein); they have valves to prevent the backflow of blood.

stem: The tiny, thin-walled blood vessels where exchange of substances between blood and cells occurs are the:
solution: Capillaries are extremely thin-walled, narrow blood vessels connecting arteries and veins; their thin walls allow the exchange of oxygen, nutrients and waste between the blood and body cells.

stem: The rhythmic beating of the heart felt at the wrist or neck is called the:
solution: The pulse is the rhythmic throbbing felt in the arteries (e.g. at the wrist) caused by the beating of the heart; the pulse rate equals the heart rate.

stem: The instrument used by doctors to listen to the heartbeat is the:
solution: A stethoscope is used by doctors to listen to the sounds of the heartbeat and breathing, helping to check the health of the heart and lungs.

stem: The excretory system removes ______ from the body.
solution: The excretory system removes metabolic waste products (such as urea, excess salts and water) from the body, keeping the internal environment clean and balanced.

stem: The main organs of excretion in humans that filter waste from the blood are the:
solution: The kidneys are the main excretory organs; they filter waste products (mainly urea) and excess water and salts from the blood to form urine.

stem: The waste liquid produced by the kidneys is:
solution: The kidneys filter the blood and produce urine (containing urea, excess water and salts), which is stored in the urinary bladder and then removed from the body.

stem: Water and dissolved minerals are transported in plants through tubes called:
solution: Xylem is the tissue that transports water and dissolved minerals from the roots upward to the leaves and other parts of the plant.

stem: Food (prepared in the leaves) is transported to other parts of the plant through tubes called:
solution: Phloem is the tissue that transports the food (sugars) made in the leaves to all other parts of the plant, including the roots, in a process called translocation.

stem: The loss of water from plants in the form of vapour, mainly through the stomata of leaves, is called:
solution: Transpiration is the loss of water as water vapour from the aerial parts of plants (mainly leaves, through stomata); it helps pull water up from the roots and cools the plant.

stem: Transpiration helps in the ______ of water from the roots to the leaves.
solution: Transpiration creates a 'transpiration pull' — as water evaporates from the leaves, it pulls water upward from the roots through the xylem, aiding the transport of water and minerals.

stem: The absorption of water and minerals from the soil in plants occurs mainly through the:
solution: Water and minerals are absorbed from the soil mainly by the root hairs, which greatly increase the root's surface area for absorption.

stem: In humans, the transport of blood in a fixed path (heart → body → heart) is called:
solution: Humans have a closed circulatory system in which blood flows through a network of blood vessels (arteries, veins, capillaries) in a fixed path, pumped by the heart.

stem: Which statement about blood is correct? (i) RBCs carry oxygen (ii) WBCs fight infection (iii) Platelets help clotting
solution: All three are correct: red blood cells carry oxygen, white blood cells fight infection, and platelets help in blood clotting.

stem: The process of removing waste and toxins from the blood is essential because their build-up would be:
solution: Excretion is essential because the accumulation of metabolic wastes (like urea) would be toxic and harmful to the body, so they must be continuously removed.

stem: Some aquatic animals and unicellular organisms remove wastes directly by:
options: Diffusion across the body/cell surface into the surrounding water
solution: Unicellular organisms and many simple aquatic animals remove waste products directly by diffusion across their body or cell surface into the surrounding water.

stem: Sweat glands in the skin help in excretion by removing:
options: Water, salts and some urea (as sweat)
solution: Sweat glands in the skin excrete sweat, which contains water, salts and small amounts of urea; sweating also helps cool the body.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a plant tissue with its function? (i) Xylem – transport of water (ii) Phloem – transport of food
solution: Both are correct: xylem transports water and minerals from roots to leaves, and phloem transports the food made in leaves to other parts of the plant.

stem: The overall importance of transportation in animals and plants is that it:
options: Ensures all cells receive food, water and oxygen, and wastes are removed
solution: Transportation systems ensure that every cell of an organism receives essential materials (food, water, oxygen) and that waste products are carried away and removed — vital for the organism's survival.

stem: The heart pumps oxygen-rich blood to the body and oxygen-poor blood to the lungs; keeping these separate is important because it:
options: Ensures efficient oxygen supply to the body
solution: The four-chambered heart keeps oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor blood separate, ensuring that the body efficiently receives oxygen-rich blood — important for animals with high energy needs.
